Subject: PulseCare RFP + initial pricing concerns

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks promising. Our procurement and finance teams reviewed the draft order form and Exhibit D (pricing table) and surfaced a few items we'd like redlined before moving to procurement approval: 

- True-up timing: can we move the true-up to 30 days after quarter close instead of 60? Our fiscal ops prefers shorter windows.
- Onboarding credit: we'd like the onboarding credit to apply for the first 9 months (to cover rollout across clinics).
- Packaging / bundling: can we get an explicit price for the 3-pack clinician bundle (we want predictable per-clinic unit costs as we pilot).
- Commit floor: the current minimum feels high for our pilot. Is there a way to build a staged floor that ramps over the first year?

I've attached a cleaned RFP and a summary redline from our procurement team (PulseCare_RFP_Q3.pdf). Please advise what you're willing to concede and any language you need from legal.

Attachment: PulseCare_RFP_Q3.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Leah Park

Subject: Re: PulseCare RFP + initial pricing concerns

Leah — thanks for the clear list. We want to keep momentum; below are options we can provisionally accept and the trade-offs we'd need: 

1) True-up window: we can accept 30 days if the customer agrees to a one-time 45-day grace for the first quarter of a pilot (to allow for onboarding delays).

2) Onboarding credit: we can extend an onboarding credit to cover up to 6 months of committed spend (rather than 9) in exchange for a guaranteed minimum annualized commitment (MAC) after month 9. The MAC would be defined as the annualized committed tokens at the end of month 9.

3) Packaging: we'll add an explicit SKU row in Exhibit D for the 3-pack clinician bundle at a set per-unit rate for the first 12 months; after that it reverts to the standard per-seat rate or the then-current promotional pricing.

4) Staged floor: propose a ramp: 25% of the annual MAC for months 1-3, 50% for months 4-6, 75% for months 7-9, and full MAC thereafter. If actual usage is below the staged floor for two consecutive quarters, standard true-up applies.

I'll loop in Legal (Neha) for concrete redline language; sales ops (Karthik) will share updated pricing workbook and the OrderForm_v3_redline with the Exhibit updates.

I've attached a working draft of the order form with placeholders (PulseCare_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) — note the Exhibit D SKU and the provisional ramp language.

Attachment: PulseCare_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (pdf)

Subject: RE: PulseCare RFP + initial pricing concerns — proposed legal language

Marissa / team / Leah — putting proposed redline language below for the key commercial points. I've attached a live pricing workbook that Karthik can use to show P&L impact.

1) True-up / grace period
Proposed clause: "Customer shall provide actual usage reports within thirty (30) days following the end of each quarter. For the first calendar quarter following Service Commencement, the parties agree to a one-time, extended reconciliation period of forty-five (45) days. Failure to reconcile within the applicable period shall not waive Seller's right to invoice for the deficiency under Section X (True-Up)."

2) Onboarding credit duration / eligibility
Proposed clause: "Seller shall apply an onboarding credit equal to 50% of Customer's monthly committed fees for the first six (6) months following Service Commencement, subject to Customer achieving the Staged Floor thresholds in Exhibit D. The onboarding credit is non-transferrable and applies only to charges invoiced for active SKUs during the credit period."

3) Staged floor (ramp) and shortfall calculation
Proposed clause: "Staged Floor: The parties agree a staged minimum commitment as set forth in Exhibit D (25% months 1-3; 50% months 4-6; 75% months 7-9; 100% thereafter). If Customer's billed usage for a rolling consecutive two-quarter period is below the applicable staged floor, Seller may invoice the difference (Shortfall) calculated as the difference between the Staged Floor amount and actual billed usage, subject to a materiality threshold of $5,000 per quarter. Shortfalls shall be invoiced at Seller's then-current list price unless otherwise specified in Exhibit D."

4) Packaging / bundle SKU definition
Proposed clause: "3-Pack Clinician Bundle: Defined in Exhibit D as a discounted SKU (BundleSKU-3C). Bundle pricing is guaranteed for twelve (12) months from Service Commencement and will be listed as a separate line item on invoices."

Risk notes (legal): 
- Recommend removing language that permits immediate termination solely for missed monthly floors during the staged period; instead allow for cure/notice and one remediation quarter before termination rights.
- Confirm that onboarding credits are accounted for in MRR calculations to avoid downstream compensation disputes.

Attachment: pricing_workbook.xlsx (xlsx)

If these are acceptable, I'll produce a PDF redline that can be shared externally.

Neha Kapoor

Subject: Re: PulseCare RFP + initial pricing concerns — closing on order form

Marissa / all — thanks for the thoughtful counter-proposals and the proposed legal language, Neha. We're close. A few final asks from the PulseCare finance team before we can approve: 

- True-up window: we'll accept the 45-day first-quarter grace, but can we standardize on 30 days thereafter? That matches our ERP timing.
- Onboarding credit: PulseCare can accept 50% for 6 months if Redwood agrees to a cap of $75,000 total onboarding credit across the contract (we need a not-to-exceed number for internal approvals).
- Bundle pricing: please include the 3-pack clinician bundle as a named SKU and indicate whether the bundle counts toward the MAC.

If you can confirm the 30-day ongoing true-up, the $75k onboarding cap, and whether bundle counts toward MAC, we can route the redline to procurement and lock the signatures. Please send the final redline PDF and a DocuSign packet when ready.

Marissa (inline): we can accept 30 days ongoing if PulseCare agrees to the $75k onboarding credit cap and we add a clause that bundles count toward MAC unless explicitly excluded in Exhibit D. I'll prepare the final redline and the DocuSign link once you confirm.

Looking forward to wrapping this up.

Best,
